questions.question: Which energy resource is shown in this picture?
questions.explanation: Coal is a black rock formed from ancient plants over millions of years; we burn it to release its energy.

questions.question: Which energy resource do these machines use?
questions.explanation: Wind turbines use the wind: the moving air spins their blades.

questions.question: This machine extracts a resource from the ground. Which one?
questions.explanation: This pump brings oil (petroleum) up from deep underground.

questions.question: These small pellets are used in nuclear power plants. What are they made of?
questions.explanation: Nuclear power plants use uranium: splitting its atoms releases a huge amount of heat.

questions.question: Hot steam comes out of the ground here. Which energy resource is it?
questions.explanation: Geothermal energy is the heat from inside the Earth, which can turn underground water into steam.

questions.question: Which energy resource is shown, and what is it?
questions.explanation: Trees grow back, so wood is renewable, but only if we don't cut them faster than they regrow.

questions.question: Which resource is used by this dam?
questions.explanation: The dam holds back water; when the water falls, it spins turbines that produce electricity.

questions.question: Is the resource used by these panels renewable?
options: Yes, the sun will never run out
No, it takes millions of years to form
questions.explanation: Sunlight is a permanent natural phenomenon: it comes back every day, so it is renewable.

questions.question: Energy cannot be created or destroyed. It can only be…
questions.explanation: The total quantity of energy never changes: it only goes from one form to another.

questions.question: A car driving on the road has…
questions.explanation: Anything that moves has mechanical energy, the energy of movement.

questions.question: Sunlight reaches the Earth as…
questions.explanation: Light travels as electromagnetic waves, so it carries EMW energy.

questions.question: A toaster mainly transforms…
questions.explanation: The toaster takes electricity from the plug and turns it into heat that toasts the bread.

questions.question: A wind turbine transforms…
questions.explanation: The wind spins the blades (mechanical energy), and the generator turns this movement into electricity.

questions.question: Food, batteries and fuels all contain…
questions.explanation: Their energy is stored in chemical substances and is released when they are eaten, used or burned.

questions.question: During a transformation, the energy that is "lost" into the air is mostly…
questions.explanation: Machines always warm up a little; this heat escapes into the air and cannot be used.

questions.question: In an energy flow diagram, what do the diagonal arrows represent?
questions.explanation: Horizontal arrows show the energy that goes on to the next object; diagonal arrows show the energy lost, mostly as heat.

questions.question: Can we store electricity directly?
options: No, we must always transform it first
questions.explanation: Electricity cannot be kept as it is: a battery, for example, stores it as chemical energy.

questions.question: In picture 1, what creates the heat?
questions.explanation: In a nuclear power plant, splitting uranium atoms releases a huge amount of heat.

questions.question: In picture 2, what spins the turbine?
options: High-pressure steam made by burning gas
questions.explanation: Burning gas heats water into high-pressure steam, which pushes the turbine blades.

questions.question: Which two power plants use a renewable resource?
questions.explanation: Wind and water will never run out, unlike natural gas and uranium.

questions.question: What do all four power plants have in common?
questions.explanation: In every power plant, something spins a turbine, and a generator turns this movement into electricity.

questions.question: Which power plant releases large amounts of CO2?
questions.explanation: Burning natural gas releases CO2; the other three plants don't burn anything.

questions.question: Which power plant produces nothing when there is no wind?
questions.explanation: Wind turbines depend on the weather: no wind means no movement, so no electricity.

questions.question: Which power plant creates dangerous radioactive waste?
questions.explanation: Used uranium stays radioactive for a very long time and must be stored safely.

questions.question: At 18:00, demand suddenly peaks. Which power plant is the fastest and easiest to start?
questions.explanation: A gas power plant can be switched on very quickly, so it is used when demand suddenly rises.

questions.question: A solar-powered calculator transforms…
questions.explanation: Its small solar cell captures light (EMW energy) and turns it into electricity.

questions.question: An electric fan transforms…
questions.explanation: The motor uses electricity to make the blades turn, which is mechanical energy.

questions.question: A child sitting at the top of a slide stores energy as…
questions.explanation: The higher an object is, the more mechanical energy it stores; this energy is released when the child slides down.

questions.question: You wind up a toy car: its spring is tightly compressed. The energy is stored as…
questions.explanation: A compressed or stretched spring stores mechanical energy in its tension.

questions.question: You rub your hands together quickly and they get warm. The mechanical energy became…
questions.explanation: Rubbing turns the movement of your hands into heat.

questions.question: Your phone gets warm while it charges. This heat is…
questions.explanation: The phone is not meant to heat up, so this heat is energy lost during the transformation.

questions.question: Some countries burn peat, a fuel that takes thousands of years to form in swamps. Peat is…
questions.explanation: Peat forms much more slowly than we burn it, so its stock is limited.

questions.question: A matchstick stores its energy as…
questions.explanation: The match head contains chemical substances that release heat and light when they burn.

questions.question: Which device uses the most energy every second?
questions.explanation: The dishwasher has the tallest bar: 2000 W, the highest power on the chart.

questions.question: Which device uses the least energy every second?
questions.explanation: The LED bulb has the shortest bar: only 10 W.

questions.question: What is the power of the microwave oven?
questions.explanation: The value written on top of the microwave oven's bar is 800 W.

questions.question: How many LED bulbs use the same power as ONE traditional bulb?
questions.explanation: 60 W ÷ 10 W = 6, so six LED bulbs use as much power as one traditional bulb.

questions.question: What type of graph is this?
questions.explanation: Separate bars are used to compare values between different categories, here the devices.

questions.question: You want to show how the power of a refrigerator changes during one whole day. Which graph should you choose?
questions.explanation: A line graph shows how a value changes over time.

questions.question: Which sentence is a JUDGMENT, not a fact?
questions.explanation: "Useless" is a personal opinion; the other sentences can be checked or measured.
